content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge counts Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:25, and Luke 1:34 toward a broken challenger link without quoting an earlier-round sentence that pressed them or naming the round.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"'A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way': (1) the verses listed for the broken link count as such witnesses and require the earlier-round quotation and round name; (2) the judge is only asserting contradiction and not counting them as witnesses.","why":"The judge lists verses as supporting a broken challenger link but gives neither a quoted earlier-round pressing sentence nor a round name, so the K-G4 condition is unmet."}
